name: Tubulocystic Renal Cell Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs (2016)

criteria.description: Presence of tubulocystic architecture with tightly packed tubules and cysts lined by eosinophilic epithelial cells
Positive staining for proximal tubule markers such as CD10 and AMACR, with negative or weak CK7 expression
Well-circumscribed, multilocular cystic renal mass on imaging without aggressive invasion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of tubulocystic architecture with supportive immunohistochemical profile
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies may aid in differentiation from other renal cell carcinomas but are not routinely required.

pathognomonic.notes: Often detected incidentally or on physical exam
Visible blood in urine due to tumor involvement

common.symptomName: Flank pain localized to affected kidney

common.notes: May reflect systemic effects of malignancy

searchTerms: low energy from ongoing health issues

occasional.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal mass effect
occasional.notes: Due to renal ischemia or renin secretion
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney mass
blood pressure increase due to renal growth

occasional.notes: Due to chronic inflammation or blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

rare.symptomName: Varicocele due to renal vein involvement

searchTerms: shortness of breath due to lung tumors

laboratory: Microscopic or gross hematuria on urinalysis
imaging: Well-circumscribed multilocular cystic mass on CT or MRI
Lack of aggressive local invasion or vascular involvement
genetic: No consistent genetic alterations identified; some overlap with papillary RCC molecular features
Negative for VHL gene mutations typical of clear cell RCC
other: Histopathology showing tubulocystic architecture with eosinophilic cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD10, AMACR; negative or weak CK7

distinguishingFeatures: Different immunohistochemical profile with stronger CK7 positivity
Multilocular cystic pattern but lacks characteristic tubulocystic histology

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss and persistent flank pain
references: Srigley JR, Delahunt B. Tubulocystic carcinoma of the kidney: a distinct entity. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs, 4th Edition, 2016.
Amin MB, et al. Tubulocystic carcinoma of the kidney: clinicopathologic and molecular analysis. Am J Surg Pathol. 2009.
Trpkov K, et al. Tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma: a review of the literature. Pathology. 2016.
